title: ios-build-processes
responsibility: Owns the ios-build-processes build or maintenance script.

inputs.name: followed.command
inputs.description: The program and arguments to run: element 0 is the executable and the rest are its arguments, run directly without a shell, with `desktopRoot` as its working directory and stdin ignored. An empty array, or a first element that is an empty string, makes `spawn` throw, so `followed` rejects before any child starts.

outputs.name: followed
outputs.description: The run's result, resolved once the child has closed or reported an error and the observation of what it started has finished: `code` is its exit code, `output` is its stdout and stderr in arrival order, and `left` is why the build could not wait for its processes, or null. A child killed by a signal or one that fails to start, such as a program that cannot be found, resolves with code 1 rather than rejecting, and `code` is never 0 while `left` is set.

examples.left: The build was stopped while processes it started still ran; none was signalled.

errors.name: TypeError
errors.description: Thrown before any child starts when `command` is missing, or when its first element is missing or empty and `spawn` refuses it. Because `followed` is async, the caller receives it as a rejection of the returned promise.
